blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Cebu City must resolve questions over its authority to use national roads for the proposed Carbon Night Market before it can institutionalize the nightly operation, councilors said during a public hearing earlier this week. At issue is whether the city can legally close portions of national thoroughfares without prior clearance from the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH). The proposed ordinance, authored by Councilor Mikel Rama, seeks to designate portions of streets in the Carbon Market area as a temporary landing and vending site for farmers, traders, and ambulant vendors.
